analyses.name: U.S. Bancorp
analyses.verdict: The tightest base in a 523-name universe, at a 52-week high, on 11x forward earnings — the single best risk/reward setup in today's scan.

financials.summary: U.S. Bancorp's FY2025 was the year the post-2023 deposit-cost squeeze finally reversed. Net interest income returned to growth as funding costs rolled over faster than asset yields, while the fee engine — payment services, trust and investment management, and mortgage banking — carried an unusually large share of revenue for a bank this size and cushioned the rate transition. Credit stayed orderly: charge-offs normalized off cycle lows rather than deteriorating, and the reserve build was provisioning for growth, not for stress. Capital finished the year comfortably above requirements, which is what funds the buyback that supports the per-share numbers. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
analyses.verdict: A $950B bellwether closing exactly at its 52-week high after a six-contraction base — the largest-cap A+ setup in the scan and the safest way to own the rotation's leading sector.

financials.summary: FY2025 was another record year, and the composition mattered as much as the total. Net interest income stayed elevated as the balance sheet repriced, but the standout was the return of capital-markets activity: investment banking fees recovered from a multi-year trough while markets revenue held near cycle highs. The consumer bank delivered steady card and deposit economics with credit costs normalizing rather than breaking. Asset and wealth management continued its quiet compounding of fee-based flows. Reserve builds reflected loan growth and a cautious macro overlay, not observable deterioration, and the fortress balance sheet again funded a large buyback plus a dividend increase. analyses.name: GE Aerospace
analyses.verdict: The cleanest large-cap industrial in the scan — a five-contraction A+ base at the high with near-unanimous TradingView confirmation, and a 41x multiple that is the one thing to respect.

financials.summary: The first genuinely clean year as a pure-play aerospace company after the GE Vernova and GE HealthCare separations, and it validated the structure. The economics are dominated by the aftermarket: spare parts and shop visits on a large installed base of LEAP and CFM56 engines carry far higher margins than original-equipment sales, and as the LEAP fleet ages into its first heavy-shop-visit cycle that mix keeps improving. Commercial Engines & Services drove both revenue and margin expansion; Defense & Propulsion Technologies grew more slowly but added backlog stability. Free cash flow conversion was strong, funding buybacks and a growing dividend. The recurring constraint was not demand but supply chain — casting and forging capacity limited how fast deliveries could ramp. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Arista Networks, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The one AI-adjacent name worth buying at the highs rather than watching — a record $3B quarter, closing at a new high on 1.8x volume while its entire cohort corrects.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the year Arista's AI networking thesis stopped being a forecast and became revenue. Ethernet won the AI back-end networking argument against InfiniBand for a meaningful share of new build-outs, and Arista's 7800-class platforms plus the EOS software stack captured much of that shift. Gross margins stayed remarkably high for a hardware company because the value sits in software and the supply chain was managed rather than chased. Cloud-titan concentration remained the structural feature of the model — a small number of hyperscalers drive a large share of revenue — but enterprise and neocloud customers broadened the base through the year. Cash generation was strong with essentially no debt. The Q2 2026 report since delivered a record $3B quarter, confirming the trajectory. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.verdict: The value expression of AI networking — 37% EPS growth at 25x with TradingView's cleanest sweep — but earnings land in 8 days, so size the position for that.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the year the Splunk acquisition stopped being a distraction and started being the story. Splunk added scale in observability and security — a recurring, software-margin revenue stream that structurally lifts Cisco's mix away from lumpy hardware refresh cycles. Underneath it, the core networking business worked through the post-pandemic inventory digestion that had depressed orders, and order growth returned. The genuinely new element was AI infrastructure: Cisco began booking meaningful orders for AI-related networking from hyperscale and enterprise customers, a business it had not previously participated in at scale. Annualized recurring revenue and subscription mix both rose. Legacy campus switching remained the drag on the growth rate. Note the fiscal calendar: FY2026 ended in July 2026 and reports on August 13, so the numbers below are FY2025. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Valero Energy Corporation
analyses.verdict: 453% EPS growth at 11x forward with an A+ base 1.5% off the high — the widest gap between delivery and multiple in the entire scan, and the peak-cycle risk that explains why.

financials.summary: FY2025 was a strong refining year and Valero is the most leveraged large-cap to that. Crack spreads stayed wide as global refining capacity additions lagged demand and several closures tightened the product balance, particularly in the Atlantic Basin. Valero's Gulf Coast complexity advantage — the ability to run cheaper heavy and sour crude and still make high-value light products — captured a disproportionate share of that margin. The renewable diesel segment, which had been a drag as credit markets and feedstock costs whipsawed, stabilized and contributed again. Capital allocation stayed shareholder-friendly: minimal growth capex, heavy buybacks against a shrinking share count, and a maintained dividend. The Q2 2026 report since showed both refining and renewable diesel surging. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Illumina, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The best turnaround setup in the scan — a six-contraction A+ base at a fresh high on 1.6x volume after a Q2 beat and guidance raise, with the earnings recovery still lagging the price.

financials.summary: FY2025 was the stabilization year. After the GRAIL divestiture removed a large cash drain and a governance overhang, Illumina refocused on the core sequencing franchise and on cost. The NovaSeq X transition — historically the source of the revenue air pocket, as customers deferred purchases waiting for the new platform and then consumed the installed base's cheaper reagents — worked through, and consumables revenue began growing again as X-series utilization ramped. Instrument placements remained the soft spot, since research budgets and pharma capex were cautious, but consumables are the annuity and they inflected. Aggressive cost restructuring lifted margins even on modest revenue growth. Bottom-line EPS was still negative year over year on our scan comparison, which is the honest gap in the story. The Q2 2026 report since beat and raised guidance. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

financials.summary: FY2025 was a year of transition managed competently. The Horizon Therapeutics acquisition delivered on its purpose: TEPEZZA and KRYSTEXXA added rare-disease revenue that partly offsets erosion in the mature base, where biosimilar competition continues to grind down legacy franchises. Repatha and the newer inflammation and oncology products grew, while several older products declined as expected. The debt taken on for Horizon was paid down steadily, restoring balance-sheet flexibility. Reported growth was modest — 4.4% EPS and 5.8% revenue on our scan comparison — so this is not a growth story; it is a re-rating story supported by pipeline optionality, principally the obesity program. Operating margins held up as cost discipline offset mix pressure, and the dividend continued growing. Exact figures render in the TradingView financials widget below.

analyses.name: Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX)
analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING — a genuine monopoly franchise at a $1.65T valuation, still 41% below its IPO-window high with no base and no valid moving averages; judge the business, wait on the price.

financials.period: No full fiscal year reported as a public company — listed roughly five weeks ago (36 trading days of price history)
financials.summary: This is the honest starting point: SpaceX has not yet reported a full fiscal year as a listed company, so there is no audited public annual statement to analyze and the TradingView financials widget will be sparse. What is publicly established about the business model: revenue comes from two very different engines. Launch services — commercial satellite deployment, NASA crew and cargo missions, and national-security payloads — is a lumpy, contract-driven business where reusability gives a cost advantage no competitor has matched, and that advantage translates into both price leadership and margin. Starlink is the opposite: a consumer and enterprise broadband subscription business with recurring revenue, high customer-acquisition and constellation-replenishment costs, and improving unit economics as the satellite count and subscriber base scale. The combination is what supports a $1.65T market capitalization at roughly 137.6x forward earnings — the market is pricing Starlink's terminal subscriber economics, not this year's launch revenue. Capital intensity is extreme: Starship development and constellation replenishment consume cash continuously.
highlights: $1.65 trillion market capitalization at approximately 137.6x forward earnings — priced for terminal Starlink economics, not current earnings
Two distinct engines: lumpy, high-margin launch services and recurring Starlink broadband subscriptions
Reusability is a structural cost advantage measured in years, not quarters, over every competitor
Only 36 trading days of price history — no valid 50-day or 200-day average, and no meaningful technical base

critical.valuation: 137.6x forward earnings for a capital-devouring business is only defensible if you underwrite Starlink's terminal subscriber economics and the launch monopoly's durability — both plausible, neither provable from 36 days of data. The franchise is genuinely worth owning; the price is still discovering where it belongs. Treat the current level as information, not as an entry, and let a base form first.
